evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: (Modern Gaelic: "Lughlagh mac Gille Chomghain", known in English simply as Lulach, and nicknamed Tairbith, "the Unfortunate" and Fatuus, "the Simple-minded" or "the Foolish"; before 1033 – 17 March 1058) was King of Scots between 15 August 1057 and 17 March 1058.

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: Lulach was the son of Gruoch of Scotland, from her first marriage to Gille Coemgáin, Mormaer of Moray, and thus the stepson of Macbeth (Mac Bethad mac Findlaích).

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: Following the death of Macbeth at the Battle of Lumphanan on 15 August 1057, the king's followers placed Lulach on the throne.

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: He has the distinction of being the first king of Scotland of whom there are coronation details available: he was crowned, probably on 8 September 1057 at Scone.

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: Lulach appears to have been a weak king, as his nicknames suggest, and ruled only for a few months before being assassinated and usurped by Malcolm III.

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: Lulach's son Máel Snechtai was Mormaer of Moray, while Óengus of Moray was the son of Lulach's daughter.

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: He is believed to be buried on Saint Columba's Holy Island of Iona in or around the monastery.

evidence.title: Lulach
evidence.text: The exact position of his grave is unknown.

evidence.text: Kaya Alp was, according to Ottoman tradition, the son of Kızıl Buğa and the father of Suleyman Shah, who was, in turn, the grandfather of Ertuğrul, and the great grandfather of the Ottoman Empire founder, Osman I.

evidence.title: Gruoch of Scotland
evidence.text: Gruoch ingen Boite  was a Scottish queen, the daughter of Boite mac Cináeda, son of Cináed III.

evidence.title: Gruoch of Scotland
evidence.text: She is most famous for being the wife and queen of MacBethad mac Findlaích (Macbeth).

evidence.title: Gruoch of Scotland
